To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ESRF Laue beamline ID09, the Daresbury software and the ESRF image intensifier type CCD are an ideal combination for Laue diffractions of protein crystals, and that this combination is the most accurate and complete Laue diffraction technique yet developed.

the use of an ESRF CCD in the Laue diffraction experiment at the ESRF ID 09 beamline from a single crystal has yielded a highly complete data set to 2.0 A resolution with high redundancy (10.7) and that the data are accurate and precise.

Laue protein crystal diffraction data can be collected from a single crystal using a CCD detector in 2.6° angle intervals, and that the data are highly complete (∞ – 2dmin = ∞; 2dmin – dmin = 91.7%), with a very large redundancy factor (11.2), which can be improved further.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of Laue diffraction methods for time-resolved studies of protein crystals.
the development of a new generation of area detectors and the development of the software algorithms to extract maximum information from these devices.
the use of synchrotron X-ray radiation in Laue geometry, with particular reference to the study of biological systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Laue crystallography is now a mature technique, with the potential to provide high-quality data for a large number of macromolecular structures.
the CCD is the detector of choice for Laue data collection.
the ESRF ID9 CCD and Daresbury Lauesoft have been demonstrated to be a highly efficient combination for synchrotron macromolecular Laue protein crystal structure determination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Laue diffraction from a single protein crystal can yield highly complete and high-resolution data, but the data quality depends on the crystal quality and the detector.
the Laue diffraction technique is now a mature method for protein crystallographers.

the Laue method using the ESRFs CCD and the DARESBURY Laue software is an extremely powerful and accurate method for obtaining high-quality protein structure data from crystals in the 10–100 kDa range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CCD is an excellent detector for the Laue method and that the Laue software is robust and accurate.
the ESRF Laue data collection technique is now a very powerful tool for protein crystallographers.
the Laue technique is now an excellent method for the determination of high-quality structures from protein crystals.
